subject: [PATCH 01/22] mm: add node-state-filtered zone and node iterators

2026-11-14.patch_summary: This patch adds helper functions and macros to the Linux kernel's memory management (mm) subsystem, allowing MM walkers to select node eligibility explicitly. It introduces nodemask intersection and nodemask/state iterators using bitmap intersection helpers without allocating temporary nodemasks. The patch includes new macros for iterating over zones on nodes in a specific state, enabling more efficient and targeted memory allocation.

reviews.author: Richard Cheng
reviews.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng questioned the consistency of two helper functions in the patch: for_each_zone_node_state and for_each_populated_zone_state, noting that the latter uses a single statement with an if/else form to avoid a -Wdangling-else warning, while the former is split into two separate functions. He asked whether the warning was significant enough to warrant keeping the current implementation or changing for_each_populated_zone_state to match.
reviews.raw_body:
A question on consistency. This one is a single for statement, with 2 new helper functions.
for_each_populated_zone_state() in the same patch uses "if (!cond) ; else" form instead.

Both forms keep a caller's else correct. The only difference I can find is that the if/else
form give a -Wdangling-else warning when the loop is the unbraced body of an if.

Is that the reason for the 2 helper function here? If the warning doesn't matter, this could
use the same short form and drop the 2 functions. If it does matter, should
for_each_populated_zone_state() be a single statement too ?

Best regards,
Richard Cheng.

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges a warning from checks and plans to re-examine and possibly restructure their code, specifically considering using a different shape or avoiding the existing pattern.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah I was getting that warning from various checks. I'd convinced
byself this was a false-positive, but it does look very funky indeed.

Let me look into this again, it's possible I can massage this better to
use the short form still.  It's also possible that I should just use a
different shape entirely than trying to use the existing pattern.

-- 
~Gregory

2026-11-18.patch_summary: This patch adds helper functions and macros to the Linux kernel's memory management (mm) subsystem, allowing MM walkers to select node eligibility explicitly. It introduces node-state-filtered zone and node iterators using bitmap intersection helpers without allocating temporary nodemasks. The patch includes new functions for iterating over zones on nodes in a specific state and defines several macros for simplifying these iterations.
